messages:
Ira M.: Hey — heads up, pre-merge CI is intermittently failing the `ci-scan` job. Seen it 3x in the last 24h, blocks merges. Error looks KMS-related (permission denied) when the scanner tries to decrypt cached artifacts. Anyone seen this?

Sam (sec): @Ira thanks. Which scanner is this (semgrep/gitleaks/snyk-code)? Can you paste the job id or last log snippet?

Ira M.: It's `semgrep` in our `ci-scan` matrix. Job id `ci-scan/2026-03-19-17:12:08`. Log snippet:

```
ERROR: PermissionDenied: requestor not authorized to perform cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.asymmetricDecrypt on projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/ci-decrypt/cryptoKeyVersions/1
  at cloudkms.v1 (kms_service.go:234)
  Caused by: Caller does not have required permission: cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.asymmetricDecrypt
```

Jen (infra): Fwiw we rolled an RBAC tidy-up on the CI service account last week (removed some broad roles). Might be related.

Alex (security): This screams IAM change. Quick triage: 1) confirm serviceAccount used by CI runner, 2) check KMS key IAM policy, 3) check recent IAM audit log for `kms.cryptoKeyVersions.asymmetricDecrypt` denies.

ops-oncall: grabbing the pipeline logs now. Also creating an incident record so we don't lose context (INC-2345).

Sam (sec): Minimal patch to unblock: add explicit binding for the CI SA scoped to decrypter role. Example (gcloud):

```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding ci-decrypt \
  --location global --keyring ci-keys \
  --member \"serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com\" \
  --role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```

Sam (sec): Better: grant a narrowly scoped principal via Terraform and include an IAM condition so the key can only be used from the CI project and by the runner SA. Something like (pseudo-TF):

```hcl
resource \"google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member\" \"ci_decrypt\" {
  crypto_key_id = \"projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/ci-decrypt\"
  member        = \"serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com\"
  role          = \"roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter\"
  condition {
    title       = \"ci-only\"
    expression  = \"request.auth.principal == 'serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' && request.time < timestamp('2026-04-01T00:00:00Z')\"
  }
}
```

Ira M.: Quick question — why is the scanner doing a KMS decrypt? I thought artifacts were stored encrypted server-side and scanners read them directly?

Jen (infra): Semgrep runner decrypts a cached encrypted bundle we store in GCS before unpacking the ruleset/artifacts. We use customer-managed keys (CMK) for that bucket. If the runner loses the decrypter privilege it fails.

Alex (security): Long-term, prefer short-lived access via Workload Identity and use a dedicated key with strict IAM. Don't give CI SA broad roles like `roles/cloudkms.admin`. Use `cryptoKeyDecrypter` only. Also add an audit filter to surface failures:

- Create a log metric for `protoPayload.methodName=\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricDecrypt\" AND severity=ERROR`
- Alert when it spikes for CI principals

Sam (sec): Also check for a latent race where KMS key rotation happened and the CI runner tried to use an old keyversion; that shows as `not found` or `wrong cryptoKeyVersion` in logs.

ops-oncall: I applied a temporary binding to unblock merges (added the decrypter role to the CI SA) and re-run the job. First re-run passed. Creating a short-lived PR to add the same change to infra Terraform. INC-2345 updated.

Alex (security): Thanks. Two follow-ups before we close the incident:
1) PR to terraform the binding with an IAM condition (no manual bindings).
2) Add audit metric + dashboard for KMS denies + link that in the runbook.
3) Confirm we don't have other services that accidentally rely on the old overly-broad role.

Ira M.: I'll open the PR today and ping for review. PR will include the TF snippet and a canary plan (run on `ci-scan` only).

Jen (infra): Note — when you add the TF resource, also ensure `google_project_iam_member` changes elsewhere won't wipe the key-level binding. We should manage the key IAM separately (dedicated TF module).

Sam (sec): I'll add a short checklist to the security runbook: 1) check KMS key policy, 2) check TF drift for key IAM, 3) add log metric, 4) prefer Workload Identity.

ops-oncall: INC-2345 set to monitoring; will close when PR merged and 48h of green CI.

Ira M.: SGTM. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

inc-bot: Incident INC-2345 created by ops-oncall, priority P2, linked to this thread.
